description:
## The smell

causal.rs spends ~669 lines (impl Replay) plus ~85 lines of shadow types reconstructing, from an ordered stream replay, a decision the scheduler already made at a specific instant.

## What is and is not already emitted

The causal ATOMS are all on the stream. work_graph.applied serializes the whole AppliedStep: changed, movements, blocked, and wakes -- each wake as {cause, job, disposition} (jsonl.rs write_wake). No field is dropped.

What is missing is the LINK. A wake says 'job J is woken by cause C'. J's own later applied event says 'J completed, here is what it read and changed'. Nothing ties J's evaluation back to C. So a consumer must re-pair them by scanning positions, which is what Replay generalizes -- and what work_graph_applied_carries_a_readable_cause_wake_evaluation_chain does by hand for a single pair.

That is why the reconstruction rule needs an interval: 'for evaluation e of F at position t, the moved inputs are (F's reads UNION F's blocked-set from its previous completion) for which a movement appears in [F's previous conclusion, t)'.

## Why that is worth fixing

- The engine does not need the interval. At enqueue_step it holds (job, cause, disposition) as a first-class Wake value: it re-ran F BECAUSE of C. 'Was this evaluation caused by new evidence?' is answerable at the moment, per evaluation, with no temporal reasoning.
- The two 'load-bearing boundaries' the module doc names -- reads alone is insufficient because waits are a separate map; the window must include the previous conclusion's own movements -- are inference rules about scheduler semantics living OUTSIDE the scheduler. Wait semantics have changed before (AND-semantics fz-go4.18.41, edge-triggered waits fz-kdt.46). A measuring instrument that silently rots when the thing it measures changes is worse than none.
- uncaused_evaluations, the exact quantity fz-kdt.34 exists to detect, becomes a direct read rather than a derived one.

## Shape

Carry the scheduling cause(s) into the evaluation record -- a correlation id on the wake that the woken job's completion echoes, or the cause identities inline. O(1) at a site that already constructs the value, behind --log-telemetry like the rest.

## Proof strategy

The existing Replay is its own oracle. Emit the link, compute the answer both ways, assert agreement across the target fixtures, then delete the replay. Correct by construction with a proof step rather than a swap on faith.

## Scope honesty

Roughly 700 lines are in play, not 2000. JSONL parsing (~71), CanonTables and canonical packaging (~213, raw ids do not survive across processes so translation at report time is real work), and the record/report surface (~550, less whatever fz-foq.6 folds) stay regardless.

## Relation to fz-foq.3

Reframes it. Before deciding where causal analysis should LIVE, decide how much of it should EXIST.

comments.text:
## Prior-art constraint this ticket must answer to (fz-kdt.34.6, commit 1c7201b9b)

The replay design is deliberate, not accidental. Its stated rationale:

- 'the scheduler stores WHICH facts a job read but never at what revision, so did this formula input move since its own prior conclusion was not answerable without adding THE SECOND DEPENDENCY LEDGER fz-kdt.34 FORBIDS.' The replay exists to keep causality bookkeeping out of the compiler.
- 'This lives entirely in the sink (CanonStream, jsonl.rs). No production emit site changed, drive.rs is byte-identical, telemetry-off renders nothing.' Zero observer effect on the system being measured.
- causal is re-exported 'because integration tests and a future trace-diff read the ARTIFACT, not the compiler' -- two logs from two processes compare, and an unplanned CI log stays analysable later.
- 'Reads a public JSONL log -- nothing else' is a forcing function proving the trace is sufficient. An in-process report could reach internal state and let the trace silently rot.

## What this rules OUT

Computing the CausalReport in-process behind a flag. It reinstates the forbidden ledger, puts analysis on the measured path, and gives up post-hoc and cross-process analysis. Do not propose it.

## What this ticket actually proposes, and its honest cost

Emit the LINK, not the report: an evaluation names the wake(s) that scheduled it. All four rationales above survive -- sink-side, log stays the artifact, trace stays self-sufficient, offline analysis unchanged -- while the interval inference disappears, because a wake that names its cause answers 'did this evaluation have new evidence?' directly.

Cost I under-stated in the description: the agenda must carry 'why is this job pending' per pending job until it runs. Transient and bounded by agenda size, cleared on run -- not a historical revision ledger -- but it IS state the compiler does not keep today. That is a real, smaller tension with fz-kdt.34's constraint and the ticket must argue it explicitly rather than assume it is free.

## Countervailing evidence for acting

Same commit: 'Both boundaries are load-bearing and both were measured red first.' The inference rule was wrong twice before it was right, and it models scheduler semantics from outside the scheduler. Wait semantics have changed twice since (AND-semantics fz-go4.18.41, edge-triggered waits fz-kdt.46). fz-kdt.34's rationale explains why bookkeeping should not live in the compiler; it does not address the external model drifting from what it models.

title: An evaluation should name the wake that scheduled it
